about: Every choice Stagecraft leaves to the person who uses it. The skill text holds principles; this file holds the settings. 'default' is what a fresh install does. 'recommend' is written for the agent: it says how to work out which value to recommend to THIS person on first launch, and what to tell them. 'applies' says where a setting acts: 'agent' (how the agent builds and publishes), 'page' (written into the page as its default; the reader can still change it in the page's own Options), 'check' (the publish check).
first_launch: Do not walk the person through this list. Read 'recommend' on each option, look at what you can see without asking (how many logins there are, which pages already exist, what kind of page they just asked for, whether they read on a phone), then show ONE short proposal grouped by the headings below: the value you would pick for them and a half-line reason, only for options where your pick differs from the default or where the choice clearly matters to them. Ask them to change any line or accept. Save what they accept with scripts/options.py set. Tell them the three ways a setting changes later: say it in plain words, change it in a page's Options panel, or edit their options file.

options.title: Which account owns a new page

choices.current: The account the working session is signed in to
choices.named: One named account owns every page (set publish.named_account)

options.recommend: Recommend 'current' to anyone who works from more than one login or workspace: a page then lives where the session that maintains it lives, a page made in one workspace starts in that workspace, and nobody has to remember an owner. Recommend 'named' only when one account must hold everything, for example a team gallery. Count the logins you can see before you speak.

options.title: The owning account when publish.home is 'named'
options.recommend: Only raise this when publish.home is 'named'. Offer the accounts you can actually see, by folder name, never by guessing an email.

options.title: What happens to a page when its session moves to another account

choices.redirect: Publish it from the new account in the same turn and replace the old copy with a short notice that links to the new one
choices.copy_only: Publish from the new account and leave the old copy as it was

options.recommend: Recommend 'redirect'. Two live copies drift apart within a day and the person ends up reading the stale one; a notice keeps every old link working. Say that the old page is replaced, not deleted: deleting is the owner's own step.

options.title: May the agent publish as an account other than the session's own

choices.off: No. If a page belongs to another account, say so and stop
choices.headless: Yes, through a headless run pointed at that account's configuration folder (see references/publishing.md)

options.recommend: Recommend 'headless' only when the person has several logins on this machine and old pages or redirect notices have to be written as their owning account. Explain in one line that it runs a second, unattended session with only read and publish allowed.

options.title: Show the page's version in its name

choices.on: The name carries the version, for example 'Bank audit v14'

options.recommend: Recommend 'on' to someone who keeps a page at one link for weeks and asks 'is this the new one?'. Leave 'off' for one-off pages.

options.title: When an existing page is published again

choices.on_change: Only when something a reader can see changed

options.recommend: Recommend 'on_change'. Accounts have a daily publish limit, and a version history full of identical pages hides the real changes.

options.title: What to say about sharing when a page is for someone else
options.default: This page is private until its owner shares it from the Share menu.
options.recommend: Ask who usually needs to see their pages and with what access, and write that into the note (for example 'Share with the finance lead as Editor'). The agent cannot share a page; the note is what it tells the person to do.

options.title: How much of the window a page uses

choices.fill: The whole window, up to layout.max_width_px

options.recommend: Recommend 'fill' for dashboards, trackers, review lists and anything with a table: empty margins beside a cramped table are the most common complaint. Recommend 'reading' only for pages that are prose from top to bottom.

options.title: The widest a page grows on a very wide screen
options.recommend: Leave the default unless the person uses an ultrawide monitor and says lines get too long, or says the page looks lost in the middle of the screen.

options.title: How wide a paragraph of text is

choices.match: As wide as the block it belongs to or introduces, so it lines up with the cards and tables around it
choices.measure: Held to a comfortable line length even when the content around it is wider

options.recommend: Recommend 'match'. A narrow paragraph stacked above full-width cards reads as a layout mistake: half the row is empty and the text wraps to five lines. If the person cares about line length, pair 'match' with layout.spare_width 'side_by_side' so a long intro shares its row with something useful instead of being squeezed.

options.title: How many characters wide a capped paragraph is
options.recommend: Only matters when text blocks are set to 'measure' or a page is a reading page. Leave 75 unless the person reads long prose on a very wide screen (try 85) or has asked for narrower columns.

options.title: What to do with width that the content does not need

choices.side_by_side: Put short blocks next to each other (an intro beside its links, cards in more columns)

options.recommend: Recommend 'side_by_side'. It keeps more of the page above the fold without shrinking anything.

options.title: Spacing
options.recommend: Recommend 'compact' to someone who reads long tables all day on a desktop; 'comfortable' otherwise. The reader can switch per page.

options.title: Clear space kept between the page content and anything that floats at an edge (the detail slider, the data dates), on both the left and the right
options.recommend: Leave the default unless the person says floating controls crowd the content (raise it to 40 or 48) or that the margins waste space on a small laptop (lower it to 20). A page that fills the window must still stop short of its floating controls by this much.

options.title: How a table row is laid out

choices.one_line: Each record stays on one line; header text may wrap

options.recommend: Recommend 'one_line' to anyone who scans or compares rows (finance, review lists, logs): the eye follows a row only when it is one line. Recommend 'wrap' for tables that are really notes in a grid.

options.title: What a column does when one field holds long text

choices.shrink_then_widen: First a smaller font in that column (down to tables.min_font_px), then a wider column, and only then a cut with the full text in a tooltip
choices.cut: Cut it with the full text in a tooltip

options.recommend: Recommend 'shrink_then_widen'. One long note column otherwise takes the width that the numbers need. If the person has trouble with small type, raise tables.min_font_px instead of changing this.

options.title: The smallest font a long-text column may shrink to
options.recommend: Raise to 12 or 13 for a person who mentions eyesight, a small laptop or reading from a distance.

options.title: What a wide table does on a narrow screen

choices.drop_columns: Hide the least important columns, with a chip to bring them back
choices.page_scroll: Let the whole page scroll sideways
choices.stack: Turn each row into a small card

options.recommend: Recommend 'drop_columns' and tell the person the agent marks which columns matter most. Recommend 'stack' if they mostly read on a phone.

options.title: A table gets a filter box once it has more than this many rows
options.recommend: Leave the default. Mention it only if they ask why a short table has no filter.

options.title: Let the reader move and hide columns
options.recommend: Leave 'on'. Turn it off for pages shown on a shared screen where a stray key should not rearrange the table.

options.title: Open a page with summary cards that filter its table
options.recommend: Leave 'on' for anyone who opens a page to answer 'how many' or 'how much' before they read rows.

options.title: The currency figures are in unless a page says otherwise
options.recommend: Set it from the person's books or locale. Do not guess; if you cannot tell, ask.

options.title: Decimals on money
options.recommend: Recommend '0' for dashboards and summaries, '2' for anything a person reconciles to the cent. If they do both, keep '0' here and let reconciliation pages set their own.

options.title: How a negative amount is written
options.recommend: Keep 'parentheses' unless the person asks for a minus sign: a negative in parentheses cannot be mistaken for a dash or a range, and it is what anyone who reads financial statements expects. Offer 'minus' to someone whose pages are engineering or scientific figures. The reader can also switch it for one page in that page's Options panel.

options.title: Where the currency is named

choices.totals: Once, on card totals and table totals, where the eye lands first

options.recommend: Recommend 'totals'. Recommend 'every' when a page mixes currencies.

options.title: Decimals on percentages
options.recommend: Leave the default unless the person works with rates where the second decimal matters (tax, interest).

options.title: Light or dark
options.recommend: Leave 'auto'. The reader can pin one per page.

options.title: Text contrast
options.recommend: Leave 'high'. It costs nothing and helps on a dim laptop or a projector.

options.title: Page colours

choices.workspace: A colour per account or workspace, from reader.palette_map, so a glance says where a page lives

options.recommend: Recommend 'workspace' to a person with several accounts who names them by colour or asks 'which account is this page on?'. Ask what they already call each one and use those names.

options.title: Account or workspace name to colour name
options.recommend: Fill only when reader.palette is 'workspace'. Use the names the person already uses.

options.title: How a tooltip opens

choices.auto: Hover with a mouse, tap on a touch screen

options.recommend: Leave 'auto'. Recommend 'click' for a person who reads on a tablet or keeps tooltips open while comparing.

options.title: How freely the agent writes tooltips

choices.generous: Every abbreviation, derived figure, status word and terse header
choices.sparse: Only what a newcomer could not guess

options.recommend: Recommend 'generous' when other people read the pages; 'sparse' for a person who is the only reader and knows the terms.

options.title: How far back a figure's sparkline goes when the history exists
options.recommend: Leave the default. History that does not exist is never invented, whatever this says.

options.title: The detail level a page opens at
options.recommend: Recommend '0' or '1' for a person who wants the answer first, '2' for someone who audits.

options.title: The Log tab (questions answered, versions)

choices.hidden: There, but hidden until the reader turns it on

options.recommend: Leave 'on' for pages that change over time; 'off' for one-off pages.

options.title: Keyboard shortcuts
options.recommend: Leave 'on'. Turn off for kiosk or shared-screen pages.

options.title: Shortcuts and Options stay in reach while scrolling

choices.on: Repeat them at the left edge, or in a thin strip on a narrow window

options.recommend: Leave 'on' for long pages. Recommend 'off' for short pages that fit one screen, or when the person finds the edge of the page too busy.

options.title: The list of shortcuts: floating and remembered, or a plain drop-down

choices.on: The Shortcuts control toggles the list under itself, in the left band under the Shortcuts tab when there is room, and the page remembers whether it was open
choices.off: The Shortcuts control toggles the list under the control in the page only (never in the left band), and the page forgets it on reload

options.recommend: Leave 'on'. Recommend 'off' when the person never wants the page to reopen a list they left open, or reads on a narrow window where the left band never fits. The list itself needs the keyboard shortcuts (reader.shortcuts) on; the left band also needs the floating tabs (reader.floating_menu).

options.title: Whether a reader can change the keys of the shortcuts

choices.on: Options has "Bind Shortcuts": the reader presses a key button, then the new key, and the choice is kept for that reader
choices.off: The keys are fixed as the settings give them; "Bind Shortcuts" is greyed out and says why

options.recommend: Leave 'on'. Recommend 'off' for a kiosk, a shared screen, or a page whose keys have been taught to a team and must not drift. Works with reader.shortcut_keys, which gives the starting keys.

options.title: Starting keys for the shortcuts, by shortcut id
options.recommend: Fill only when the person has told you the keys they want (for example {"options": "g", "theme": "Ctrl+Shift+D"}). The ids are in the page's Bind Shortcuts list and in PB.keys.all(): shortcuts, options, theme, detail-less, detail-more, filter, tab-prev, tab-next, tab-1 to tab-9, method, item-next, item-prev, approve, hold, strike, send, comment, copy-csv, restore-columns, hide-column. A key the browser keeps for itself (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, F5 and the like) or one that two shortcuts would share is ignored with a warning. An empty string means no key. Not for secrets or for text.

options.title: Where a link to another Claude page opens

choices.browser: A new tab in the same browser
choices.app: The installed Claude app, when the browser hands links to it

options.recommend: Keep 'browser'. Look for an installed Claude app (a Chrome or Edge web app, or the desktop app): when one is installed, a plain new-tab link to a Claude page is taken by the app, which pulls the reader out of the browser they were working in and often into another login. Recommend 'app' only to someone who says they read their pages in the app. The reader can switch it for one page from the page's own controls.

options.title: What the page header says about who made it

choices.full: Author session name and id, whether a session is watching, how old the data is
choices.name: Author name and data age only

options.recommend: Recommend 'full' to anyone running more than one session: it answers 'who do I ask about this page, and is anyone there?'. Recommend 'name' for pages sent outside the team, where a session id means nothing.

options.title: Where a page shows how current its data is (one 'data through' date, or one per source when there are several)

choices.float_right: A small block that floats at the right edge and stays in view while the page scrolls
choices.float_left: The same at the left edge

options.recommend: Recommend 'float_right' to anyone who acts on the numbers: the first question about any figure is 'as of when?', and the answer should not need a scroll to the top. Recommend 'header' for short pages that fit one screen. The dates themselves are not optional; only their place is.

options.title: Where the agent asks for a quick answer, a ruling or an override about something on a page

choices.page_first: On the page (an ask card or a rulings table), with one line in chat saying it is there

options.recommend: Recommend 'page_first' to a person who reviews from the page or away from the terminal: the answer is saved, signed and waits for the session. Recommend 'chat' if they never open pages while a session runs.

options.title: A countdown with Undo after a click

choices.when_item_moves: Only where the click makes the row or card leave or move, so the reader keeps their place
choices.never: Never; a click is saved at once

options.recommend: Recommend 'when_item_moves'. A timer on a click that changes nothing on screen only makes the page feel slow.

options.title: Length of that countdown, in seconds
options.recommend: Leave the default.

options.title: What the publish check does with a page that skips Stagecraft

choices.remind: Publish it and print what is missing
choices.refuse: Refuse until it is fixed or marked exempt

options.recommend: Recommend 'remind' for the first weeks. Recommend 'refuse' once the person has said twice that a page ignored their settings: at that point a reminder is not doing its job.

options.title: A Method tab that explains how the page was made, for a reader with no context

choices.required: A page that shows data and has no filled Method tab is refused
choices.recommended: Publish it and remind the author

options.recommend: Leave 'recommended' for the first weeks. Recommend 'required' for a person whose pages are read by others later (an accountant, a successor, a new agent that has no access to the sources): a page that cannot say where its figures came from, and which numbers were typed in or assumed, is hard to trust or rebuild. Recommend 'off' for throw-away pages. The Method tab is plain text in the page's source, with fixed sections; see references/components.md.

options.title: One-line notes that tell the person which setting shaped a page and how to change it
options.recommend: Leave 'first_pages'. The point is that the person learns the settings are theirs; after that the notes are noise.
